learning_outcomes.text: To acquire sufficient capacity to design, direct, and maintain industrial or residential building installations for their correct use, within the parameters established by current regulations.
Learn to handle technical-legal documentation: laws, technical regulations, technical standards.
Structure standard calculation procedures through robust engineering methods for quality implementation in installation design, based on known physics, legal framework, and technological experience.

syllabus_topics: Thermal Insulation of Equipment and Ducts

assessment_methods.method: Tests of theory, calculation exercises, laboratory practices, and assignments during the course

assessment_rules: The course evaluation is divided into three components: in-course tests (20%), a final written exam on Part I (40%), and a final written exam on Part II (40%). For the final written exams (Parts I and II), a minimum score of 5.0 out of 10 is required in each part to pass. Partial exams can eliminate material from the final exams if a score of 5.0 or higher is achieved, and these scores are saved for both exam calls. If a student's average grade is 5.0 or higher but they have not met the minimum score in either Part I or Part II, the final grade will be 4.9 (Fail). Students who have passed may retake the exam to improve their grade, with the best score being considered.
